subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

body:
From: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@nordholm-payments.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Tobias Richter <t.richter@richter-partners.de>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 09:18 AM CET
Subject: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the security review earlier this month.

Attached are our counsel’s redlines on the MSA/DPA. The main points we need resolved before we can move to signature:

1) Data residency: EU-only processing/storage for any “Customer Content” and any logs that could contain personal data.
2) No cross-region failover for Hosted without explicit written consent.
3) Incident notification: we require notice within 24 hours of discovery for any security incident impacting our data.

Could you please confirm if Redwood can agree to the above (or propose alternative language)?

Best,
Lena

—
Lena Vogt
Procurement Manager | Nordholm Payments

Attachment: Nordholm_Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:02 AM CET
Subject: Fwd: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Naomi — looping you in for quick guidance before I respond.

Key asks from Nordholm (DACH payments, regulated):
- EU-only processing/storage for “Customer Content” AND any logs that could contain personal data.
- Explicit: no cross-region failover for Hosted unless written consent.
- Incident notification: 24h from discovery for any security incident impacting their data.

Questions for you (and Security, if you’ve already aligned):
1) For Hosted w/ region pinning: are we comfortable committing to “Customer Content processed only within allowed region(s)” and what do we say about logs/traces/metrics? Their counsel is pushing hard on “any logs that could contain personal data.”
2) Incident notification: do we have an approved standard (e.g., without undue delay / 72h) and are we willing to agree to 24h in the MSA? If not, what compromise do we usually offer?
3) Subprocessors/support access: do we need any callouts for access from US-based engineers (even if data remains in EU)?

Attaching redlines for context.

Thanks,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
EMEA Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Nordholm_Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 08:36 AM CET
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Thanks — here’s the current approved position we can put in contract language (aligned w/ Security, but keeping this to what we can safely commit today).

1) Data residency scope
- We can commit that “Customer Content” (prompts, inputs, uploaded files, and model outputs) for Hosted is processed and stored only in the pinned region(s) when region pinning is enabled.
- We should NOT commit that *all* telemetry/logs are EU-only in absolute terms. The right wording is that we do not route/store Customer Content outside the pinned region(s), and that operational logs exclude Customer Content by default. Some metadata (request IDs, timing, error codes) may be processed in global systems. If they insist, we can offer a stricter “EU telemetry tier” only if SRE signs off (not standard).

Suggested language (short):
“Provider will process Customer Content solely within the Allowed Region(s) configured for Customer’s account. Provider’s standard operational logs are designed to exclude Customer Content; such logs may include limited metadata (e.g., request identifiers, timestamps, and performance metrics) and may be processed in other locations.”

2) No cross-region failover
- Agree in principle: if pinned EU-only, we should say we will not perform cross-region failover for Customer Content. Exception only if Customer config allows multiple Allowed Regions.

Suggested language:
“Provider will not transfer or process Customer Content outside the Allowed Region(s), including for failover purposes, unless Customer has configured multiple Allowed Regions.”

3) Incident notification
- Our standard is “without undue delay” and we typically target 72 hours for confirmed breaches; 24h from discovery is hard because we may have incomplete info early.
- Compromise that has worked: “promptly, and in any event within 72 hours of confirmation of a Security Incident involving Customer Content,” plus an initial notice sooner “as reasonably practicable.”

Suggested language:
“Provider will notify Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a confirmed Security Incident involving Customer Content, and will provide updates as information becomes available.”

If they insist on 24h, we can propose:
- 24h for “High severity incidents with confirmed impact to Customer Content,” not for any suspected/ongoing issue.

4) Support access
- Don’t volunteer US support access language unless asked. If asked: we can say access is controlled, audited, least privilege; but it’s not a residency violation if data remains in EU.

If you want, I can send you a one-page “residency addendum” draft (we used similar in another EU payments deal) to attach.

Naomi


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@nordholm-payments.eu>
Cc: Dr. Tobias Richter <t.richter@richter-partners.de>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 11:12 AM CET
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Hi Lena (hi Dr. Richter),

Thanks for sending the redlines — we can meet the intent on residency and propose a few edits to align with how the Hosted service operates.

Data residency (Hosted, with region pinning enabled)
- We can agree that Customer Content (prompts/inputs + outputs) is processed only within the Allowed Region(s) configured on your account (e.g., EU-only).
- We can also agree that we do not process Customer Content outside the Allowed Region(s) for failover purposes, unless you configure multiple Allowed Regions.
- On logs/telemetry: our standard operational logs are designed to exclude Customer Content. They may contain limited metadata (request ID, timestamps, performance metrics, error codes) and some of that metadata may be processed in global systems.

Incident notification
- We can commit to notification without undue delay after we become aware of a confirmed Security Incident involving Customer Content, with follow-up updates as information becomes available.
- Your proposed “within 24 hours of discovery” is difficult to sign as written (often we don’t have confirmation or scope inside 24h). If helpful, we can propose a compromise where 24h applies to high-severity incidents with confirmed impact to Customer Content.

To make this easy, I’m attaching a short “Data Residency Addendum” draft we can use as a rider (or we can incorporate the same language into the DPA).

Would you like to jump on a 20 min working session early next week to close the remaining wording?

Best,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
EMEA Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Data_Residency_Addendum_v1.pdf


From: Dr. Tobias Richter <t.richter@richter-partners.de>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@nordholm-payments.eu>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 14:48 PM CET
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Dear Ms. Schmitt,

Thank you for the proposed addendum. We appreciate the clarifications.

We still have two points that need adjustment:

1) Logging/metadata.
Your language permits processing “metadata” in global systems. For a payments processor, some identifiers may qualify as personal data, and therefore we require that any logs relating to our usage remain within the EEA.

2) Incident notification.
We understand your concern on premature notification. However, our regulator expects notification within 24 hours of becoming aware of an incident that could affect confidentiality/integrity of customer data. We can accept “initial notification” within 24 hours with limited information, followed by updates.

Additionally, please confirm whether Redwood personnel located outside the EEA can access our environment (even if the data is hosted in the EU).

Kind regards,

Dr. Tobias Richter
Rechtsanwalt | Richter & Partners


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Tobias Richter <t.richter@richter-partners.de>
Cc: Lena Vogt <lena.vogt@nordholm-payments.eu>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 25, 2025 at 16:07 PM CET
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — MSA/DPA redlines (data residency + incident notification language)

Dear Dr. Richter (and Lena),

Understood — thanks for spelling out the regulatory driver.

On the three open items:

1) Logs/metadata in EEA
We can propose revised language that distinguishes:
- “Customer Content” (always confined to Allowed Region(s) when pinning is enabled), and
- “Service metadata” (request IDs, timestamps, latency/error codes) which is designed to exclude Customer Content.

We cannot commit today that *all* service metadata is processed exclusively within the EEA for the Hosted service in all cases (some centralized systems are global). If EEA-only logging is a hard requirement, the two paths we can offer are:
(a) adjust configuration to minimize/disable certain telemetry fields and retention (where supported), and/or
(b) evaluate a Dedicated / private deployment where we can scope telemetry processing more tightly.

If you can tell us which specific identifiers you consider personal data in this context (e.g., end-user IDs embedded in headers, IP addresses, etc.), we can align on an approach to ensure those do not enter logs.

2) Incident notification timing
We can accept “initial notification within 24 hours” provided it is framed as an initial notice based on preliminary information, with a commitment to provide ongoing updates as we confirm scope and impact. Proposed wording:
“Provider will provide an initial notification to Customer without undue delay and, in any event, within twenty-four (24) hours after becoming aware of a Security Incident that is reasonably likely to involve Customer Content. Provider will provide additional information and updates as it becomes available.”

3) Personnel access outside EEA
Yes, Redwood may use personnel located outside the EEA for support and security operations. Access is controlled via least-privilege roles, audit logging, and approval workflows. This does not change where Customer Content is processed when region pinning is enabled.

If helpful, Naomi (Product/Security) can join a short working call to walk through the above and confirm what we can commit in the DPA vs. in a security exhibit.

Proposed times (CET): Wed 11:00–11:30 or Thu 15:00–15:30.

Best regards,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
EMEA Enterprise | Redwood Inference

CC: Naomi Feldman | Product, Security & Compliance
CC: Avery Johnson | Enterprise Account Executive
